A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the brain accumulation of the EGFR inhibitor osimertinibs is limited by efflux via ABCB1 and to a lesser extent ABCG2, but that this does not affect the oral availability and does not result in a high toxicity risk.

The main takeaway from our work is that
ABC transporters are not a limiting factor for osimertinibi brain accumulation and oral availability.
ABC transporters do not limit the efficacy of osimertimib in the brain and that the drug can be safely administered at a higher dose to improve efficacy.

the ABCB1 and/or ABCG2 efflux transporters are not likely to be a major barrier for oral osimert inib brain penetration, and therefore inhibition of these transporters is unlikely to be a useful approach to improve the brain accumulation of this drug.
